title: Publish taskfast-cli to crates.io (enable cargo publish job in dist)
description:
The README advertises `cargo install taskfast-cli --locked` but the crate has never been published to crates.io (badge: 'not found', package page 404). Root cause: dist-workspace.toml has `publish-jobs = ["homebrew"]` with NO cargo job, and release.yml never runs cargo publish.

CRITICAL DECISION NEEDED BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: publishing the CLI requires all 4 workspace crates to be on crates.io (taskfast-client 0.3.0, taskfast-chains 0.1.0, taskfast-agent 0.7.0, taskfast-cli 0.7.0) because they are versioned path-deps. cargo publish fails if a path-dep is unpublished unless it is publish=false. The team must decide: (a) publish all 4 as public crates, or (b) mark the 3 internal crates publish=false and restructure. Option (a) leaks internal crates (irreversible); option (b) requires refactoring the CLI's dep edges.

Plan (assuming option a):
1. Confirm all 4 crates have crates.io-required metadata (description/license/repository/homepage/keywords/categories). taskfast-cli has it; verify the other 3.
2. Enable the cargo publish job: dist-workspace.toml -> publish-jobs = ["homebrew", "cargo"], then `dist generate` to regen release.yml (repo has allow-dirty=["ci"]).
3. Add CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN repo secret (Settings -> Secrets); dist reads it by default.
4. Flip the cargo-semver-checks baseline in ci.yml (~line 130-132, there is an explicit TODO comment 'Switch to the default crates.io baseline after first publish'): drop --baseline-rev $BASE_SHA, use published baseline.
5. Dry-run locally: cargo publish --dry-run -p taskfast-cli (and deps).
6. Ship via existing taskfast-cli-vX.Y.Z tag -> release.yml now runs cargo publish.

Risks: first publish is irreversible (versions yankable but not deletable). Token secret must exist before next release tag.

Verification: curl https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/taskfast-cli returns version; cargo install taskfast-cli --locked works.

Files: dist-workspace.toml, .github/workflows/release.yml (regenerated), .github/workflows/ci.yml (semver baseline), repo secrets.
notes:
REAL PUBLISH ATTEMPTED — blocked by crates.io account email verification.

Dispatched publish-crates.yml dry_run=false (run 28210970639). taskfast-codegen upload FAILED with HTTP 400:
  'A verified email address is required to publish crates to crates.io. Visit https://crates.io/settings/profile to set and verify your email address.'

Root cause: the crates.io account that owns the CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN has no verified email. The token + secret are fine; the account just needs email verification (one-time account setting).

SIDE BUG FOUND + FIXED: the workflow's 'already published' detection was masking this error. It ran 'cargo publish --dry-run' on failure and treated exit 0 as 'already published' — but --dry-run succeeds for any cleanly-packaging crate, so it false-positively printed 'already published; skipping' and hid the real 400. Fixed in 98d9e5b: rewrote to query the crates.io sparse index for the exact version BEFORE uploading (skip-if-exists), so completed crates are skipped on re-run without ever masking a real failure. Added index-propagation wait between topological steps.

BLOCKER (maintainer-only, one-time):
1. Log into crates.io with the account that owns the token, go to https://crates.io/settings/profile, set + verify the email address.
2. Re-dispatch publish-crates.yml dry_run=false. It will now publish codegen -> client -> chains -> agent -> cli in order, skipping codegen if the earlier partial upload actually landed (sparse-index checked), and surface any real error honestly.

Nothing else is pending on the code side.
close_reason:
DONE. All 5 crates published to crates.io and 'cargo install taskfast-cli --locked' verified working end-to-end (binary runs: taskfast 0.7.0).

Published versions (confirmed via crates.io sparse index): taskfast-codegen 0.1.0, taskfast-client 0.3.0, taskfast-chains 0.1.0, taskfast-agent 0.7.0, taskfast-cli 0.7.0.

Final publish run: 28213093254 (green). The idempotent skip logic confirmed re-runnable: 4 crates skipped as already-published, taskfast-cli uploaded.

Two real bugs found & fixed during publish (both same class: build-time/embedded file paths escaped the cargo package root, breaking publish verification):
1. taskfast-client/build.rs read spec/openapi.yaml via ../../ — bundled the spec into crates/taskfast-client/spec/ (06fe99f), vendor-spec.sh + check-spec-drift.sh keep it synced.
2. taskfast-cli skills.rs embedded skills/taskfast-agent via ../../ — bundled into crates/taskfast-cli/skills/ (52b55ea), validate-skill.sh keeps it synced.

Crates.io account email verification was the other gate (user-resolved). publish-crates.yml now publishes in topological order, idempotently, with honest error propagation (98d9e5b).

title: Fix RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN auth failure in bump.yml checkout
description: 'Release bump' workflow_dispatch run 28346830523 (2026-06-29) failed at actions/checkout's fetch step: 'fatal: could not read Username for https://github.com: terminal prompts disabled'. Raw job log confirms secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN resolved NON-empty (checkout successfully wrote the AUTHORIZATION extraheader) — so this is a REJECTED credential, not a missing/empty one. User confirmed the PAT itself is current/not expired, ruling out simple expiry. Root cause is one of: (1) the RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN secret's stored value is stale — PAT was rotated after the secret was last updated (2026-04-17 per gh secret list) without pushing the new value in, (2) the fine-grained PAT's repository-access scope no longer includes Akuja-Inc/taskfast-cli, or (3) org-level PAT approval was revoked independent of the token's own expiry. Workaround already applied in PR #87/#88 (manual local bump) for v0.9.0.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm which of the 3 causes applies (check secret's Updated date vs PAT rotation date, PAT repo-access scope, org PAT approval list), refresh RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN accordingly, and get a green workflow_dispatch run of bump.yml on main (checkout, bump, tag, push, and release.yml triggers).
close_reason: Root cause was wrong — RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN is current, not expired. Full raw log shows actions/checkout's auth setup (extraheader + includeIf.gitdir) completed without error; the subsequent git fetch still ran with no credentials applied ('could not read Username...terminal prompts disabled' is a client-side no-creds error, not a server auth rejection). This is a one-off actions/checkout credential-wiring glitch, likely tied to that day's runner image (git 2.54.0), not a bad/expired secret — 9/10 prior runs on the same token succeeded. No action needed unless it recurs; if bump.yml fails the same way again, worth pinning an older actions/checkout version or explicitly clearing any global credential.helper before the checkout step.

title: Tighten workspace dep floors so minimal-versions passes on modern nightly
description:
Follow-up to tfcli-3xe. The minimal-versions advisory job (now in ci-scheduled.yml) still does not pass because the workspace has many loosely-floored deps that let -Z minimal-versions resolve to ancient transitive crates which don't compile on modern nightly. tfcli-3xe stopped this from reddening the gating badge by moving the job; THIS issue makes the job actually green.

Confirmed broken transitive chains (from local minimal-versions reproduction on nightly 1.98.0 2026-06-17):
- clap 4 -> 4.5 FLOOR BUMPED in tfcli-3xe (eliminated rustix 0.36 via is-terminal 0.4).
- anyhow 1 -> 1.0.95 FLOOR BUMPED in tfcli-3xe (old anyhow 1.0.0 fails on modern rustc: StdError::backtrace trait change).
- eth-keystore -> uuid 0.8 -> getrandom 0.1.7 (broken: cfg-if 0.1 macro error). Needs eth-keystore floor bump or uuid floor.
- reqwest -> mime_guess 2.0.0 + old unicase (broken: FromStrError does not implement Display). Needs mime_guess/unicase floor pin.
- tempfile 3 (dev-dep) -> rand 0.7 -> getrandom 0.1 (dev-only, not built by 'build --workspace' but is by --all-targets).

Approach: tighten direct-dep floors in Cargo.toml so -Z minimal-versions resolves each to a version whose own transitive tree compiles on MSRV 1.95. Candidates to review: eth-keystore, tempfile, rand, uuid, reqwest, serde/serde_json, tokio, futures, chrono, rust_decimal, and the alloy-* crates. For pure-transitive offenders (mime_guess, unicase) add an explicit workspace.dependencies floor.

Verification: cargo +nightly update -Z minimal-versions && cargo +nightly build --workspace --locked -> green. Then optionally re-gate minimal-versions into ci.yml.

Discovered-from: tfcli-3xe.

title: Fix flaky minimal-versions scheduled CI job (rustix 0.36.4 build break)
description:
The weekly scheduled `minimal-versions` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (~line 179) is failing, which drives the CI badge red. Root cause is NOT in this repo's code: `cargo +nightly update -Z minimal-versions` downgrades rustix to 0.36.4 (oldest in the ^ range), which fails to compile on current nightly with: `error: cannot find attribute rustc_layout_scalar_valid_range_start in this scope` (rustix-0.36.4/.../errno.rs). Failed run: 27941318458 (2026-06-22). Note this job is schedule/dispatch-only and never gates PRs, so push CI is green.

Recommended fix (Option A1): lift the broken rustix floor in the workflow by pinning rustix back up after the minimal-versions downgrade, e.g. add `- run: cargo +nightly update -p rustix --precise 1.1.4` between the update and build steps. Lowest blast radius, matches standard ecosystem practice.

Alternatives: (A2) pin nightly to a known-good date via rust-toolchain.toml; (A3) make minimal-versions non-blocking in notify-discord (worst - hides signal).

Verification: `gh workflow run ci.yml -f` dispatch -> green; next scheduled Monday run green.

rand 0.9 is BLOCKED in taskfast-cli: alloy-signer-local v1 + eth-keystore 0.5 require a rand_core 0.6 RNG in PrivateKeySigner::encrypt_keystore (taskfast-agent/keystore.rs:140). rand 0.9 = rand_core 0.9, incompatible trait. Unblocks only on alloy v2 migration. dependabot ignore added in PR #60. Also: rand is an unused dep in taskfast-client.

alloy crates do NOT share a version line. The upper-layer crates (alloy-consensus, alloy-signer, alloy-signer-local, alloy-eips, alloy-network, rpc/provider) version together at 2.x; the foundational alloy-primitives and alloy-sol-types stay at 1.x (alloy-consensus 2.0.5 depends on alloy-primitives 1.x — there is NO 2.x of primitives/sol-types). So a 'bump alloy to v2' = set consensus/signer/signer-local/eips to "2", keep primitives/sol-types at "1". v2 needed zero source changes in taskfast-cli; keystore still takes a rand 0.8 RNG under alloy-signer-local 2.0.5 (so this did NOT unblock rand 0.9 / gh#25).
